subject: Coordination: traffic rehearsal & access checklist for Q3 streaming test
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj@zenithsystems.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@zenithsystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coordination: traffic rehearsal & access checklist for Q3 streaming test

Hi Raj / Claire —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good sync. Per our discovery, you want a customer-driven rehearsal that validates both batch throughput and streaming concurrency for your transcription pipeline (end-to-end from client SDK -> Redwood hosted inference). I captured the outcomes and proposed plan below so we can lock the window.

Summary of objectives
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 400ms for non-streaming generation at 1k token sequences
- Streaming: sustain 350 concurrent streaming sessions (50–100 tokens/sec average per session) with end-to-end tail latency p95 < 600ms
- Throughput: peak sustained 700 req/s (small payloads) for short bursts up to 1.2k req/s
- Success criteria: no more than 1% request error rate, no service fallbacks triggered, and end-to-end SLOs met for 90% of the 30-minute run window

Proposed rehearsal plan
1) Pre-flight (48–24h): exchange allowlist IPs and create test accounts; Redwood provides test API keys and a sandbox model variant pinned for the rehearsal.
2) Smoke (T-1h): 10-minute smoke to validate connectivity and credentials.
3) Main window (30 mins): Three 10-minute phases — ramp, sustain, ramp-down. We'll run both k6 (synthetic short requests) and Locust (streaming websocket sessions) concurrently.
4) Post-mortem (T+1h): share metrics (token counts, error rates, pXX latencies) and next steps.

Action items for Zenith (what we need from you)
- Confirm window (2–4 hour slots on Aug 25–27 UTC preferred)
- Provide public IPs for allowlist: CSV in the attached allowlist_template.csv
- Provide sample streaming client config (concurrency target & token rate) or grant us access to your client repo link so we can mirror it in Locust.

Attachments I’m including: rehearsal-checklist.md (step-by-step), allowlist_template.csv, and sample locust scripts (locust-scripts-v2.zip).

Ben (cc'd) will send the sandbox API key and the k6/Locust orchestration instructions. Soojin will own the telemetry dashboards during the run.

Proposed next step: can you confirm which day (Aug 25, 26, or 27) works and share the allowlist CSV by EOD Monday?

Thanks —
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj@zenithsystems.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@zenithsystems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordination: traffic rehearsal & access checklist for Q3 streaming test

Grace — thanks for the clear summary. Claire and I reviewed this and we’re aligned on goals. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Window: Aug 26 UTC 16:00–16:45 (we prefer evening US hours so our on-call can shadow) — can you confirm Redwood can support that slot?
2) IPs: I attached the current egress CIDRs from our fleet. We also have a small NAT range for test runner VMs; I added that to the attached.
3) Streaming client: we will share a trimmed-down client config (concurrency target = 350 sessions, token rate target = 80 tokens/sec avg per session) by EOD Sunday. If Redwood needs the repo access, I can add a read-only deploy key.
4) Sandbox data: we’ll use an internal test corpus (anonymized transcripts). No PHI.

One ask: do you have guidance on local backpressure handling for the SDK? We saw some retransmits in an earlier rehearsal. If there’s a best-practice config you recommend, please include that.

I’ve attached the allowlist file (zenith_allowlist_aug26.csv).

—Raj
Director, Platform Engineering
Zenith Systems

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj@zenithsystems.com>, Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@zenithsystems.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordination: traffic rehearsal & access checklist for Q3 streaming test

Thanks Raj — Aug 26 16:00 UTC works for our infra team. Quick technical notes and what I’m sending over now:

Sent in this thread: 1) sandbox API key (redacted in this email — actual key pushed to customer vault) 2) repo link to locust orchestration and k6 scripts: https://drive.redwood.com/zenith/rehearsal/locust-v2 (see runbook README for orchestration flags) 3) small helper script for simulating SDK backpressure behavior (backpressure-helper.py)

Important infra/config guidance
- API rate model: we recommend a client-side retry cap of 2 retries with exponential backoff (100ms -> 500ms) and circuit-breaker window of 10s for transient spikes.
- Streaming sockets: enable keepalive of 60s and limit per-IP socket concurrency to 450 on the Redwood side for the rehearsal (we’ll monitor).
- KV cache warmup: if you can seed the cache with a sample prefix set we’ll reduce cold-start token latencies. We’ll coordinate details via the repo.

Credentials & access
- Sandbox API key: redwood-sandbox-zenith-aug26 (pushed to your secure vault — let us know if we should email it instead)
- Test user account: zenith_test_user_01 (use for auth headers in the scripts)

Pre-flight checklist (run T-48 to T-1h)
- Confirm allowlist (received)
- Verify API key access (Ben)
- Smoke run (T-1h) — recommended command: ./run_smoke.sh --target http://sandbox.redwood.ai --key <vault-key>
- Monitor dashboards: link to Grafana provided in runbook

I’m attaching locust-scripts-v2.zip and the rehearsal-checklist.md here for convenience.

If anything changes on Zenith's side re: CIDRs or token rates, flag it ASAP. We’ll stand up a Zoom at T-15m and post the run metrics live to the shared drive link.

-Ben
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: locust-scripts-v2.zip, rehearsal-checklist.md

From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@zenithsystems.com>

Subject: Re: Coordination: traffic rehearsal & access checklist for Q3 streaming test

All good on our end — Aug 26 16:00 UTC confirmed. We added the deploy key for the repo (read-only) and uploaded the trimmed streaming client config to the Drive link you shared (filename: zenith_streaming_config_v1.json).

We’ll have our on-call (Martin Lee) in the run and Claire will be the primary contact. Expect the allowlist to be finalized in the file you received; I updated one of the NAT ranges (see row 7).

One more note: if during the run you observe sustained tail latency increases beyond p95 thresholds, please trigger the pre-agreed fallback to the lower-fidelity model variant and notify us immediately — we’ll accept temporary quality degradation to preserve availability.

See you Monday for the pre-flight smoke (T-1h).

Thanks —
Claire
Sr. Engineering Manager
Zenith Systems
